corpus.content: Merge sort divides the array recursively and merges sorted halves. Its time complexity is O(n log n) in all cases (worst, average, and best).
In our initial analysis, the instructor stated that merge sort runs in O(n^2) worst case.
Excuse me, I made a mistake earlier when I said O(n^2). Merge sort is actually O(n log n) because the recurrence relation T(n) = 2T(n/2) + O(n) solves to n log n.
corpus.correction_reason: Verbal correction by instructor correcting prior slip

corpus.content: Binary search requires a sorted array and runs in O(log n) time complexity with O(1) auxiliary space.
Master Theorem applies to recurrences of the form T(n) = a*T(n/b) + f(n). If f(n) = Theta(n^(log_b(a))), then T(n) = Theta(n^(log_b(a)) * log n).
Newton's Second Law of Motion: Net force equals mass times acceleration, written as F = m * a.
Kinetic Energy of an object with mass m and velocity v is KE = 0.5 * m * v^2.
As you can see, kinetic energy is simply mass times velocity squared KE = m * v^2 without the half factor.

Visual diagram demonstrating optimization trajectories. When learning rate alpha is too large, the optimizer diverges and cost increases. When alpha is appropriate, it converges smoothly to the local minimum.
Parameter update rule: theta := theta - alpha * grad(J(theta)) where alpha is the step size or learning rate.
BFS explores graph vertices level by level using a FIFO Queue data structure. Its time complexity is O(V + E).
DFS explores deeply along each branch using recursion or an explicit LIFO Stack. Time complexity is O(V + E).
QuickSort performance depends on pivot choice. Random or median-of-three pivot avoids the O(n^2) worst case on already sorted input.
Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm requires non-negative edge weights. For graphs with negative weights, use the Bellman-Ford algorithm.

conflicts.resolution: Instructor corrected slip at 45.0s, confirming O(n log n).
Slide formula KE = 0.5 * m * v^2 is authoritative; spoken omission of 0.5 is incorrect.
